question_text: The IUPAC name of CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH₂–CH₃ is:
explanation: The longest chain has 4 carbons. Numbering from the end nearer the branch puts the methyl group on C-2.
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

question_text: The hybridisation of each carbon atom in ethyne (HC≡CH) is:
explanation: Each carbon forms two σ bonds and two π bonds, which needs two hybrid orbitals, so it is sp.
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

question_text: Which of the following carbocations is the most stable?
explanation: Stability increases with the number of alkyl groups through the +I effect and hyperconjugation: 3° > 2° > 1° > methyl.
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

question_text: Which of the following groups shows the strongest –I effect?
explanation: –NO₂ is a very strong electron-withdrawing group. –CH₃ shows a +I effect.
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

question_text: Which of the following carbocations is stabilised by resonance?
explanation: The positive charge of the allyl cation is delocalised over two carbons through the adjacent π bond.
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

question_text: A functional isomer of ethanol (C₂H₆O) is:
explanation: CH₃OCH₃ has the same formula C₂H₆O but a different functional group (ether instead of alcohol).
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

question_text: Which of the following is a nucleophile?
explanation: NH₃ has a lone pair to donate. BF₃, H⁺ and AlCl₃ are electron-deficient electrophiles.
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

question_text: Which of the following is an electrophile?
explanation: AlCl₃ has an incomplete octet and accepts an electron pair.
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

question_text: Homolytic fission of a covalent bond produces:
explanation: Each atom takes one electron of the shared pair, giving two free radicals.
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

question_text: Which of the following carbanions is the most stable?
explanation: Alkyl groups push electrons towards the negative carbon through the +I effect and destabilise it, so the methyl carbanion is the most stable of these.
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

question_text: Which of the following is the strongest acid?
explanation: Three chlorine atoms exert the strongest –I effect and stabilise the carboxylate ion the most.
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

question_text: Which of the following shows geometrical (cis–trans) isomerism?
explanation: Each carbon of the C=C in but-2-ene carries two different groups (H and CH₃).
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

question_text: Which of the following is optically active (chiral)?
explanation: C-2 of butan-2-ol carries four different groups: H, OH, CH₃ and C₂H₅.
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

question_text: Which of the following can show keto–enol tautomerism?
explanation: Tautomerism needs an α-hydrogen. Only acetone has one of these four.
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

question_text: The IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂CH(OH)CH₃ is:
explanation: The OH group gets the lowest locant (2) in the four-carbon chain.
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

question_text: The IUPAC name of CH₃–CH=CH–CHO is:
explanation: The aldehyde carbon is C-1, so the double bond between C-2 and C-3 gives but-2-enal.
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

question_text: Which of the following is aromatic?
explanation: The cyclopentadienyl anion is planar, cyclic, fully conjugated and has 6 π electrons (4n + 2 with n = 1). The cation and cyclobutadiene have 4 π electrons and are antiaromatic.
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

question_text: In the acetate ion, the two C–O bonds are:

options.A: one single and one double bond of different lengths
options.B: identical in length, between a single and a double bond

explanation: Resonance delocalises the negative charge over both oxygens, so the two C–O bonds are equivalent.
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

question_text: The IUPAC name of (CH₃)₃C–CH₂–CH₃ is:
explanation: The longest chain has 4 carbons, and the two methyl groups sit on C-2 when numbered from the end that gives the lower locants.
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

question_text: A meso compound is optically inactive because of:

options.A: a racemic mixture of two enantiomers
options.B: internal compensation due to a plane of symmetry
options.C: the absence of any chiral centre in every case
options.D: the presence of a double bond

explanation: A meso compound has chiral centres, but the rotation of one half cancels that of the other because of an internal plane of symmetry.
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

question_text: Which of the following free radicals is the most stable?
explanation: Alkyl groups stabilise radicals by hyperconjugation, so the order is 3° > 2° > 1° > methyl.
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

question_text: Which of the pentane isomers has the highest boiling point?

options.D: all have the same boiling point

explanation: Branching makes the molecule more compact and reduces the surface area for van der Waals forces, so the unbranched isomer boils highest.
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

question_text: Which of the following are electrophiles?
explanation: BF₃, H⁺ and NO₂⁺ are electron-deficient. NH₃ has a lone pair and acts as a nucleophile.
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

question_text: Which statements about resonance are correct?

options.A: Contributing structures differ only in the arrangement of electrons
options.B: The resonance hybrid is more stable than any single contributing structure
options.C: The contributing structures are separate isomers in rapid equilibrium
options.D: All contributing structures have the same positions of atoms

explanation: Resonance structures are not real isomers. The molecule is a single hybrid of all of them.
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

question_text: The number of structural isomers of C₄H₁₀ is:
explanation: They are n-butane and 2-methylpropane (isobutane).
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

question_text: The number of structural isomers of pentane (C₅H₁₂) is:
explanation: They are n-pentane, 2-methylbutane and 2,2-dimethylpropane.
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

question_text: The number of σ bonds in a molecule of propene (CH₃–CH=CH₂) is:
explanation: There are 6 C–H σ bonds and 2 C–C σ bonds (the C=C contributes one σ and one π), which gives 8.
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

question_text: The number of α-hydrogens available for hyperconjugation in the tert-butyl cation, (CH₃)₃C⁺, is:
explanation: Each of the three methyl groups attached to the positive carbon has 3 hydrogens, so 3 × 3 = 9.
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

question_text: The total number of stereoisomers of tartaric acid (2,3-dihydroxybutanedioic acid) is:
explanation: There are two optically active enantiomers (d and l) and one meso form.
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

question_text: The number of sp² hybridised carbon atoms in CH₂=CH–C≡CH is:
explanation: The two carbons of the C=C are sp². The two carbons of the C≡C are sp.
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
